description: Macro Evaluation Rewrite — replace template-substitution macro expansion with staged compilation (real VM evaluation at expansion time) via a reentrant jacl_context_t. Includes 7-byte name limit fix as prerequisite. Internal jacl_ctx_run API is shared substrate for future M14 [interpret $src] builtin.

userStories.title: Hygiene de-risking spike
userStories.description: As the implementer, I need to validate the proposed mark-propagation hygiene rule before touching any compilation code, so that the rewrite doesn't unravel on a wrong assumption.
acceptanceCriteria: Pick 5-8 representative templates from test_m10 (must include: simple unquote, ~@ splicing, ^-prefixed identifiers, gensym use, nested syntax-quote, identifier capture/shadowing, transitive macro composition)
For each template, hand-lower the syntax-quote body into a tree of make-syntax/vec calls as it would compile under staged eval

Run hand-lowered bodies through the existing VM with the proposed mark-propagation rule: 'currently-executing macro call has a current_mark in its frame; every make-syntax call during that frame applies the mark to the output; spliced-in arg syntax objects pass through unchanged with their existing marks'
Diff the resulting syntax trees against today's expand__subst_template output for the same templates — output must be byte-identical (modulo position metadata)
Document any divergence cases and propose updated rule
If no rule produces byte-identical output for all templates, STOP and re-evaluate Option A before continuing this PRD
Spike output captured at .ralph/spikes/macro-eval-hygiene-spike.md with templates, lowered forms, diff results, validated rule
No production code modified; spike code lives under .ralph/spikes/ or is reverted before US-002 begins
Build passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Spike captured at .ralph/spikes/macro-eval-hygiene-spike.md. 7 representative templates (simple unquote, ~@ splicing, ^-prefix, gensym, nested syntax-quote, identifier shadowing, transitive composition) hand-lowered to make-syntax trees and traced under proposed mark-propagation rule. All 7 byte-identical to today's expand__subst_template output. One refinement: caret-marked nodes always carry mark 0 regardless of frame mark. Decision: proceed with PRD.

userStories.title: Fix jacl_inline_string silent truncation
userStories.description: As the runtime, I want jacl_inline_string to refuse strings longer than 7 bytes rather than silently truncating, so that bugs in name handling fail loudly instead of producing corrupted identifiers.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_inline_string(s, len) in src/value.c (around line 293) becomes a precondition: if len > 7, hit a JACL_ASSERT(len <= 7, ...) instead of 'if (len > 7) len = 7;'
All callers of jacl_inline_string audited; any that might pass len > 7 are updated to either pre-check or route through jacl_string_new instead
Existing test suite still passes
Assertion never fires under normal use after the audit
Build passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Replaced silent truncation with fprintf+abort assertion. Audited all callers: only embed.c:608/615 (embed__register_native) were unsafe — now route through jacl_intern for names > 7 bytes. All other callers pre-guard or use constant strings <= 7 bytes.

userStories.title: Remove 7-byte name limit at compiler binding sites
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to use variable names longer than 7 bytes (captured, counter, current, element) without the compiler rejecting them, so I can write idiomatic code.
acceptanceCriteria: All 14 enforcement sites in src/compiler.c (lines ~3355, 3366, 3640, 3653, 3730, 4172, 4722, 4859, 5335, 5480, 6099, 6428, 7668, 8034) modified to no longer reject names > 7 bytes
Each binding site uses jacl_string_new(heap, intern_table, name, len) instead of jacl_inline_string(name, len) to construct the JaclVal name for Local/Upvalue/GlobalArity
Names <= 7 bytes still produce inline strings (cheapest representation)
Names 8-128 bytes produce interned strings (pointer-stable, == comparison still works)
Names > 128 bytes are rejected with clear error 'variable name exceeds 128-byte limit' (rope strings are not pointer-stable)
compiler__resolve_local, compiler__resolve_upvalue, compiler__find_global, sm__find_field continue to use JaclVal == comparison unchanged
Verify pointer-stability of interned strings via test

Add integration tests exercising long variable names in: def, mut, set!, proc params, vec destructure, named destructure, struct spread, for binding, try binding (each test uses a name in the 8-30 byte range)
Add a test verifying the 128-byte hard cap rejects with the expected error
Add a test verifying that two def sites at different scopes with the same long name resolve correctly (proves interned string identity works)
Build passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added compiler__name_val helper routing <=7 to inline, 8-128 to interned, >128 rejected. Refactored ~12 analysis functions (analyze__walk_body, analyze__collect_procs, compiler__analyze_suspension, sm__walk_suspensions, ast__contains_suspension, compiler__top_level_suspends, ast__collect_local_muts, ast__contains_nonlocal_set, ast__collect_local_names) to accept heap/intern_table params and use compiler__name_val instead of jacl_inline_string. Fixed VM OP_GET_GLOBAL error message to use jacl_string_data for interned names. 16 integration tests in test_long_names.c covering all binding sites and boundary conditions.

userStories.title: Expand gensym prefix capability
userStories.description: As a macro author, I want to give gensym a descriptive prefix like 'loop_idx' instead of being capped at 3 bytes, so generated names are debuggable.

userStories.notes: Expanded jacl_gensym_next to accept prefixes up to 64 bytes (was 3). Names formatted as prefix__counter; <=7 bytes use inline strings, longer use jacl_intern. Added JaclInternTable* param to jacl_gensym_next and threaded through expand__subst_template. Updated expand__is_gensym_call to accept prefixes up to 64 bytes. userStories.title: Define jacl_context_t and audit VM reentrancy
userStories.description: As the implementer, I need a reentrant execution-context type that owns the arena, GC heap, intern table, macro table, and VM state, so that compile+run cycles can be nested (macro expansion to VM, future interpret to VM).
acceptanceCriteria: Define jacl_context_t struct in a new header (e.g. src/context.h or in src/jacl.h) that owns: arena_t, ThreadHeap, JaclInternTable, MacroTable, VM, and a restriction_set placeholder field (uint64 bitmask, all-permissive default)
Provide jacl_ctx_new(parent_ctx) (parent may be NULL for root) and jacl_ctx_destroy(ctx) lifecycle functions
Child contexts may share parent's intern table but have their own arena/heap

Audit vm_exec and all functions it transitively calls for state that assumes a single in-flight execution: file-static caches, instruction-pointer registers held across calls, signal handler globals, etc.
Document audit findings in a comment block at the top of src/vm.c or .ralph/notes/vm-reentrancy.md

Fix any reentrancy hazards found (move file-static state into VM struct fields, replace global counters with context-scoped ones, ensure no opcode handler holds state across recursive vm_exec invocations)
Add a test that calls vm_exec recursively (top-level invokes a builtin that itself calls vm_exec on a fresh closure) and verifies both invocations complete correctly without state corruption
Refactor jacl_run (src/vm.c around 6381) to construct a jacl_context_t internally rather than assembling pieces ad-hoc; public API unchanged
Resist coupling the context type to macro-specific concerns (no scope_mark fields, no defmacro registration in the struct itself)
Build passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Defined jacl_context_t struct owning arena, VM, JaclInternTable, MacroTable, ExpandState, restriction_set (uint64 bitmask, all-permissive default). jacl_ctx_new(parent) shares parent intern table for child contexts; jacl_ctx_destroy frees owned resources. Audited all .c files for file-static reentrancy hazards: found 7 in syntax.c (expand error state, frame stack, scope counter, gensym counter). Moved all into ExpandState struct threaded through expansion functions. jacl_gensym_next now takes uint32_t* counter param. jacl_run uses stack-local ExpandState. Audit documented in vm.c comment block. Two integration tests: context_lifecycle and recursive_vm_exec with independent macro expansion.

userStories.title: Internal jacl_ctx_run API
userStories.description: As the macro expander (and future interpret builtin), I need a stable internal API to compile and run JACL source or AST inside an existing context and receive a result value.
acceptanceCriteria: Provide internal API: JaclVal jacl_ctx_run_source(jacl_context_t *ctx, const char *src, size_t len, uint64_t restriction_set, JaclError *err_out) — lex, parse, compile, exec, return result

Provide internal API: JaclVal jacl_ctx_run_closure(jacl_context_t *ctx, JaclClosure *closure, JaclVal *args, uint32_t arg_count, JaclError *err_out) — invoke a pre-compiled closure with arguments and return result
Errors propagate via JaclError out-param: kind (compile-error / runtime-error), message, source position
restriction_set parameter is plumbed but not enforced beyond a no-op pass-through in this story (will be wired in a later PRD when sandboxing matters)
Add tests: invoke jacl_ctx_run_source with valid source, invalid source (compile error), source that throws (runtime error); verify each path returns the expected value/error
Add a test that nests jacl_ctx_run_source calls (an inner script that itself calls into the API via some test hook) — confirms reentrancy survives the public boundary
No user-facing interpret builtin is added — this is internal API only
Build passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented jacl_ctx_run_source (lex→parse→compile→exec pipeline) and jacl_ctx_run_closure (direct closure invocation) in vm.c. JaclError type defined in both vm.c (unity build) and jacl.h (external). 4 integration tests: valid source, parse error, runtime error, nested reentrancy. restriction_set plumbed but not enforced (per AC).

userStories.title: Compile syntax-quote as an expression
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to lower syntax-quote bodies into bytecode that constructs a syntax object at runtime via make-syntax calls, instead of representing them as static template AST.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a new compilation rule in src/compiler.c for AST_SYNTAX_QUOTE that emits bytecode constructing the templated syntax tree at runtime via OP_SYNTAX_OP (existing make-syntax subops 7-12 from US-016)

Unquoted subexpressions (~expr) are compiled as normal expressions; their resulting JaclVal (which must be a syntax object at runtime, or an auto-promoted literal) is spliced into the parent make-syntax call's args
Unquote-splicing (~@expr) lowers to a vector-flatten step in the parent's args construction; the expression's value must be a vector of syntax objects at runtime
Nested syntax-quote (e.g. syntax-quote {syntax-quote ~x}) compiles correctly: outer treats inner as a literal-ish subtree, but unquotes inside inner are still subexpressions of the outer level
The new compilation rule is ONLY used by US-008's staged path; existing macros routed through old expander are unaffected
Add a feature flag or compilation context bit that selects the new rule

Add tests: a hand-written defmacro whose body is a syntax-quote expression compiles, runs as a closure, and produces a syntax object whose structure matches expectations; cover literal substitution, ~, ~@, nested quote
Build passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added use_staged_syntax_quote flag on ExpandState + jacl_context_t. New syntax__compile_sq_node recursive function emits OP_SYNTAX_OP subops 7-12 (make-syntax) for AST_LIT_INT/FLOAT/STRING/VAR_REF/COMMAND/BLOCK, compiles ~expr as normal expressions, handles ~@expr with OP_VEC_PUSH/OP_VEC_CONCAT, and emits nested syntax-quote as constants. Gate in AST_SYNTAX_QUOTE case checks c->use_staged_syntax_quote. 4 tests: literal, unquote, unquote-splicing, nested.

userStories.title: Staged macro expansion path with per-macro routing flag
userStories.description: As the macro expander, I need a parallel staged-evaluation expansion path that compiles macro bodies as closures and invokes them via jacl_ctx_run_closure, gated by a per-macro flag so that existing macros continue using the template substituter.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a bool use_staged_eval field to MacroEntry in src/compiler.c (around line 2189) and src/jacl.h (around line 843); default false
Modify expand__node in src/syntax.c (around line 1416) to check entry->use_staged_eval per macro call: if false use existing template-substitution path, if true use new staged path

Implement the new staged path: at expansion time, ensure entry->closure is compiled (compile body via the new syntax-quote-as-expression rule from US-007), convert caller args to syntax-object JaclVals, invoke jacl_ctx_run_closure(ctx, entry->closure, args, arg_count, &err), expect a syntax-object result, convert back to AST via existing syntax_to_ast, replace the call site, and re-expand
Macro body compilation now happens interleaved with expansion, not in a later compile pass
When a defmacro with use_staged_eval=true is encountered, compile its body immediately (using the in-progress jacl_context_t) before continuing AST traversal

Forward references (a staged macro that calls another staged macro defined later in the same file) handled by two-pass approach: pre-register all defmacro names with stub entries, then compile bodies in order, then expand calls
Add a test-only mechanism to set use_staged_eval=true on a defmacro (programmatic test-harness hook preferred over parser changes)
Add at least one test macro that uses the staged path end-to-end and produces correct output; compare against the same macro on the old path; outputs must match
Hygiene is NOT yet implemented in the staged path in this story (US-009 follows); test macros in this story must be hygiene-trivial (no shadowing)
Add a test for forward-referenced staged macros (macro A calls macro B defined later in same file)
Build passes
Tests pass (none use the staged path yet except the new test macros)
userStories.notes: Added use_staged_eval field to MacroEntry. Added jacl_context_t *ctx to ExpandState. Three-phase expansion in staged mode: register all defmacros, compile staged bodies via expand__compile_staged_body, expand calls. Non-staged mode preserves original single-pass semantics. expand__node checks entry->use_staged_eval to route between template substitution and jacl_ctx_run_closure. AST_DEFMACRO compilation skips staged macros whose closures are already compiled. 3 tests: e2e comparison, block body, forward references.

userStories.title: Mark-propagation hygiene at make-syntax call time
userStories.description: As the staged expansion path, I need to apply scope marks to syntax objects constructed during a macro invocation, so that hygiene works the same as the template-substitution path.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement the mark-propagation rule validated in US-001's spike: the executing macro call has a current_mark field in its CallFrame (or in the jacl_context_t); every make-syntax invocation during that frame applies the mark to the output; spliced-in arg syntax objects pass through unchanged with their existing (caller's) marks
^-prefixed identifiers in source (set as is_caret=1 on the AST/syntax) opt out of mark application (the current mark is NOT applied to caret-marked nodes)
Update all OP_SYNTAX_OP make-syntax subops (src/vm.c lines 5979-6107) to consult the current frame's mark and apply it

When jacl_ctx_run_closure is invoked from the expander, it receives a current_mark parameter (allocated fresh per macro call by expand__scope_counter or its successor); this mark is set on the outermost frame
Migrate ALL test_m10 hygiene tests to use_staged_eval=true and verify byte-identical output against the template-substitution path
Add a regression test for any divergence found in the spike (US-001) that the new rule was updated to handle
Build passes
test_m10 passes on the staged path
All other tests still pass on the old path
Tests pass
